title: When the Ember Turns
premise: Oscar Ishikawa has spent a lifetime keeping the Ember Gate shut and the Ledger of Impossible Things balanced, trading in favors, names, and small miracles for the guild that prefers to stay invisible. When prayers begin reaching old gods who answer too literally, Oscar learns their own name was sold decades ago to the court beneath the mountain, and the soulless shell they've been living in is starting to crack. To reclaim it, Oscar must open the gate they were sworn to keep closed, bargain with a god who remembers them as someone else, and confront the guildmaster who made the original sale. In the end, Oscar chooses neither the self that was stolen nor the one imposed on them, forging a third identity from the ledger's blank pages—and sealing the gate from the inside, at a cost.
about_author: Paloma Pemberton is a former archivist who claims she once catalogued a book that catalogued her back. She writes fantasy about doors, debts, and the people paid to stand between them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unopened Doors
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A routine night balancing the ledger is interrupted by a prayer that arrives addressed to no god—except it lands on Oscar's desk anyway. The emotional beat is quiet unease: the first sign that invisibility is failing, delivered through the mundane ritual of bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered Too Well
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Across the city, answered prayers leave miracles with teeth: a widow's wish returns her husband wrong. Oscar traces each miracle to the Ember Gate's hairline cracks, realizing the old gods are using the gate as a listening post. Beat: dread sharpening into responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Guildmaster Knows
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar confronts Guildmaster Vess, who deflects with charm but lets slip a word—'Ishikawa'—spoken like an itemized debt. That night Oscar finds their own signature in a forty-year-old entry: one soul, sold beneath the mountain. Beat: betrayal and vertigo.

chapters.title: The Hollow Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Oscar and a memory-fragment of the child they were before the sale. As the soulless shell thins, Oscar loses colors, then the taste of salt, then the memory of their mother's face. Beat: grief for a self they never got to keep.

chapters.title: A Thief Hires a Thief
chapters.summary: New POV: Juno Vale, a guild thief with her own unpaid debts, is blackmailed by Vess to stop Oscar. Instead, reading the ledger's margins, she realizes Vess profited from the sale. She offers Oscar her skills. Beat: wary alliance, first spark of belonging.

chapters.title: Descent by Ledger Light
chapters.summary: Oscar and Juno's POV, alternating. They enter the mountain through a debtor's door Juno knows, navigating courts where every kindness is collateral. Oscar bargains with a minor god using entries torn from the ledger. Beat: power's seduction—Oscar enjoys bargaining more than they should.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Before the Undercourt, Oscar demands their soul back; the court agrees—for a price: another soul, freely given, or the gate opened wide so all gods may pass. Meanwhile Vess arrives to collect on Juno. Beat: the trap closes; corruption offered politely.

chapters.title: Names Are Debts
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Juno offers herself in Oscar's place, arguing a thief's soul is already half-spent. Oscar refuses and instead reveals Vess's embezzlement of soul-interest to the court, turning its own accounting against the guildmaster. Beat: fury as clarity; the corrupt devoured by contract.

chapters.title: When the Ember Turns
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, climax. The Undercourt, bound by its own terms, releases the soul—but opening the gate to carry it out lets the old gods surge through. Oscar must choose: flee whole or stay and close the gate from within. They choose to stay, becoming the gate's living hinge. Beat: sacrifice as self-authorship.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Third Name
chapters.summary: Juno's POV, resolution. Months later, prayers go unanswered because the gate holds; Juno keeps the ledger now, writing Oscar's new name on the first blank page—a name neither sold nor given, but chosen. Somewhere in the stone, something warm answers a knock. Beat: belonging found in absence.
